text: I think people sometimes abuse the term "white" to mean "generous" or "kind" or "nice". They mean it in a good way. But I hate that phrase because it has a very particular meaning. I hate when people say "white of you" because that can be a funny insult actually. "White" in modern slang, most colloquially, but still basically British, means you are elitist, you are classist, you think you are better than everybody else, you only deal with other white people, other white Americans, white British people, middle class, upper class. White people's understanding of how things are. So, if somebody does a very nice thing, they come over, they help me, they throw me a lifeline, they do me a massive favour, and I say thank you, and they say, "that was white of me, that was nice of me", it means nothing to me, because white in my mind, in my cultural understanding, is a thing that is wrong, that I don't want. And I don't want it in my life. I don't want elitism, I don't want classism, I don't want people to think they're better than me. So I really dislike that phrase. I mean I guess I wish people would say nice, or good, or lovely, or generous, or kind, or sweet, any other kind of lovely, positive thing. And only white, only when you're trying to insult somebody. That's when I like that term. That's when it belongs. That's the time to use the term. But yeah, anytime somebody says it, they get a weird, disgusted face from me. So I just stop talking to them. I walk away. I don't actually talk to them for a week. So yeah.
